time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame 0 at t = 0; time t -> frame round(24 t)
pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin at top-left pixel of the 1920x1080 frame
setting: Dimly lit underground car park (level 'B1'): concrete pillars, ceiling with long fluorescent tube lights, grey floor with green-painted front area. One yellow sports car (RX-7 style coupe, pop-up headlights, rear spoiler, white 5-spoke rims, California plate 'PSHERO') drives from the back left towards the camera and curves out to the right.

camera.evidence: phase correlation of ceiling region (x 0-1450, y 0-450) vs frame 0: |shift| <= 0.023 px in every frame
camera.horizon_evidence: two ceiling light tubes (parallel straight 3D lines) fitted y=0.15838x+187.09 and y=0.10591x+399.58 (rms <0.3 px) meet at (4050, 829); the floor colour edge y=-0.0418x+1001.9 also reaches y=829 near x~4140. The car's wheel hubs stay at y 819-845 at all distances -> camera height ~ wheel-hub height (very low camera), horizon ~ y 829. Camera roll ~0 (vertical pillar edges are vertical).
camera.focal_length: unknown - estimate from given depth_info + a known size (e.g. car length/height or wheel diameter).

events.event: first frame: car visible at back left, nearly head-on, already pulling out (moving slowly)
motion start / creeping: silhouette right edge 443 -> 443 -> 447 -> 452 (frames 0-3), so the car starts at or near rest around frame 0-1 and speeds up
car turning (yawing) continuously from facing the camera (frames 0-10) towards moving to the image right; near-side front rim first detectable
both near-side wheels visible (rear rim appears)
car broadside to the camera (hubs level, wheelbase growing fastest), front end reaches the dark zone at the foreground pillar
front end fully lost in darkness; only rear half visible
last visible frame (tail corner at right edge x 1824-1919)

no_events: no bounces, impacts, contacts or stops; single continuous drive with one gradual left turn (from the driver's view: heading towards camera -> heading to image right)
apparent_size_trend: car approaches the camera: visible silhouette length 383 px (f0, front view) -> 757 (f20) -> 1029 (f27) -> ~1240 (f30, broadside, front dark); front rim height 54 (f10, partly hidden) / 120 (f20) -> 168 (f29); rear rim 98 (f23) -> 160 (f36). Rim height (vertical, yaw-independent) is the cleanest inverse-depth cue: depth ~ f * rim_diameter / rim_h.
